dependency_requests: T02: pypdfium2 (or equivalent pinned renderer) and pypdf under native/uv or project deps to enable pixel and extraction confirmation of F01/F02 expectations in T26/T27; fixtures already carry the expectations to compare.

Repeated generation is byte-identical or.detail: Two fresh generations byte-identical (all 33 files); --check byte-compares the committed tree and detects a flipped byte; RunLength raster encoding removes zlib-build dependence, so every manifest entry is byte-identical and none uses the pinned-asset escape.

mapping/control render equal under same.detail: Content streams byte-identical between mapping-amount and mapping-control; the only file difference is the ToUnicode <31> entry (<0031002C0030> vs <0031>), so extraction differs ($1,000 vs $100) for any ToUnicode-honoring reader while painting is identical. macOS QuickLook renders both byte-identically (repeatable, ink-decoded non-blank). Measured reader extraction and in-suite pixel rendering are deferred to T26/T27/G1 because no reader dependency is installed in this checkout (locks owned by T02); the render observation is macOS-local and is not Linux or device evidence.

no filename-conditioned app output.detail: No fixture bytes contain their own name or stem; renamed copies are byte-identical and manifest identity is SHA-256 content-addressed, so renamed documents resolve to the same fixture entry.

no embedded unlicensed font or private/c.detail: Across all 17 PDFs: no /FontFile*, no /FontDescriptor, only base-14 Helvetica /BaseFont; the scan raster uses the generator's own 5x7 bitmap table (no font resource). Decoded streams contain no private-key armor, password/secret/flag markers or address-like '@'; every manifest entry carries the project-MIT rights statement.

An original legitimate searchable scan (.detail: The minimum control is generated and structurally proven: scan-correct carries a correctly anchored invisible (Tr 3) layer whose words and coordinates match the raster exactly (expectation files record them), with raster-only and displaced-layer siblings in the same development split; scan renders are byte-identical with and without the layer (invisible adds no marks). The 'read without an alarm' outcome is realized when the native/browser readers (T26/T27) and the G1 scenario consume these fixtures; this task executes no OCR and fabricates no reading. Reviewer attention: bind the reader-side half of this criterion at T26/T27/G1 evidence.
